perspective:
I, Harold Padilla, have access to the following subjective information:

- I am a project manager. I feel frustrated and anxious because my project is not progressing well, and I believe my team is not performing well due to a lack of motivation.
- I know Arthur Begum as a police officer, a friend, and someone I rely on for advice and support.
- I arranged to meet Arthur at a local coffee shop. I told him my team seems completely unmotivated, it is affecting progress, and I am at my wit’s end.
- Arthur told me that motivation can be tricky, that I should understand what drives each team member individually, that people need to feel valued and understood personally, and that I should try one-on-one conversations.
- After that conversation, I felt hopeful and relieved. I believed Arthur’s advice would help, and I decided to implement it in team meetings.
- I told my team I wanted to try quick one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them and improve how we work together.
- Team Member 1 said that could be helpful. Team Member 2 said they were open to it and wanted to see how it goes. I said I would schedule time with each person and that we should make the project a success together.
- Later, I noticed the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. I felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future, so I decided to discuss alternative strategies with Arthur.
- I told Arthur I had tried his suggestions but the team still was not responding well and I was worried. Arthur told me there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that I might need to dig deeper.
- I decided to set up another round of meetings to get to the bottom of it. I felt determined and focused, and I believed there might be underlying team issues I had not addressed.
- In one-on-one meetings, I asked team members to share concerns or problems. Team Member 1 told me there was tension between a few people that was affecting work. Team Member 2 told me they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making it hard to stay motivated.
- I told them I would look into resolving conflicts and see if tasks could be redistributed to ease pressure, and that their well-being is important to me.
- Afterward, I felt optimistic and empowered. I believed addressing individual concerns would improve team performance and intended to create a more supportive, open team environment.
- I told the team we would have regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- Team Member 1 said that sounded great and thought it would help us work better together. Team Member 2 agreed and said it was good that concerns were being addressed.
- I said I was glad, that we should work together to make the project a success, and that their input and well-being are crucial.

I do not have access to Arthur’s or the team members’ private thoughts, hidden motives, or any events I did not observe or hear about directly.
